sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *pasar a* + infinitive from B2 Unit 23: it means to move on to the next step, after something came before (*Ahora pasemos a ver los resultados*). It fits the story of Uruguay's recent changes, where one project led to the next one: first hydroelectric power, then wind; first primary school, then secondary.

sections.title: Pasar a + infinitive
rows: Después de la energía hidráulica, el país pasó a invertir en energía eólica.
*pasó a invertir*: went on to invest
Con el tiempo, el plan pasó a incluir a los alumnos de secundaria.
*pasó a incluir*: went on to include
Ahora pasemos a hablar de la energía renovable.
*pasemos a hablar*: let us move on to talking
Primero se aprobó la ley; después, el Parlamento pasó a discutir otra.
a first step, then *pasó a discutir*

items.spanish: Después de la energía hidráulica, el país pasó a invertir en energía eólica.
items.english: After hydroelectric power, the country went on to invest in wind power.

items.spanish: Con el tiempo, el plan pasó a incluir a los alumnos de secundaria.
items.english: In time, the plan went on to include secondary students.

items.spanish: Ahora pasemos a hablar de la energía renovable.
items.english: Now let us move on to talking about renewable energy.

items.spanish: Primero se aprobó la ley; después, el Parlamento pasó a discutir otra.
items.english: First the law was passed; then Parliament moved on to discuss another.

sections.content: *Pasar a* needs an earlier step to move on from, and always has *a* + infinitive. If nothing came before, use *empezar a*. It does not mean "to pass" or "to go by" here. With *ser* it says what something became: *pasó a ser*.
